title: 10 Ways To Slow Down And Sleep Well After A Long Day Of Teaching
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Facing the elevated stress of pandemic teaching, Linsin offers ten concrete techniques for winding down and sleeping better after the school day. Several are physiological — box breathing borrowed from Navy SEALs, breath holds that trigger the parasympathetic nervous system, and daily sunshine and walking — while others are behavioral, like simplifying workload, taking frequent breaks, and starting the evening wind-down early rather than prepping lessons late at night. Two techniques focus on mindset: a 'decide first' ritual in which teachers commit each morning to staying calm regardless of what happens, and visualization, in which teachers rehearse handling stressful classroom moments with composure before they occur. He closes with a Marcus Aurelius quotation on obstacles becoming the way forward, framing the whole list as evidence that stress can be actively managed rather than simply endured.
points: Use box breathing (four-count inhale, hold, exhale, hold) to calm the nervous system before or after stressful moments.
Get daily sunshine and take a walk after the workday to lower stress hormones and improve sleep quality.
Simplify your workload by discarding anything not absolutely necessary, rather than adding more systems to cope.
Use a 'decide first' morning ritual — committing in advance to stay calm no matter what the day brings.
Finish the workday early enough to genuinely disconnect, since evening lesson prep undermines sleep and recovery.
quotes: The good news is that you don’t have to put up with it. You don’t have to stand by and watch it happen to you. With a little discipline, releasing the pressure valve isn’t so hard.
The Navy SEALs famously use box breathing to calm themselves before and after missions. It clears the mind, slows the heart rate, and improves performance.
Walking has been shown to lessen feelings of anxiety, stress, and depression, increase self-confidence, and improve the quality of your sleep. It’s also a potent fat-burner.
This is one of the most powerful stress relieving strategies I’ve ever come across. And though incredibly simple, it works like magic.
The worst thing you can do is to prep for the next day of teaching in the evening. Better to be less prepared and energetic than over-prepared and in need of sleep.
The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
